name: PMMY - Mudra Loan (PM Mudra Yojana)
statusNote: Live scheme applied through participating banks and NBFCs, with MUDRA and JanSamarth portals listed.
purpose: Small business finance for eligible income-generating activities.
documents: Business address proof and registration documents
Project report or quotations, if required
process: Apply through a participating lender or eligible online channel.
Select the appropriate Mudra category and submit documents.
The lender checks credit history, business viability and repayment ability.
Complete sanction formalities if approved.
portalNote: Portals given: MUDRA https://www.mudra.org.in/ and JanSamarth https://www.jansamarth.in.
caution: Categories: Shishu up to ₹50,000; Kishor above ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh; Tarun above ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh; Tarun Plus above ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh.

name: CGTMSE Credit Guarantee Scheme
statusNote: Live guarantee scheme with its own portal, taken by the lender on your loan application.
purpose: Eligible term loans and working-capital credit supported by a credit guarantee.
documents: Bank statements and financial statements, as applicable
Project report and existing loan details
process: Approach a participating bank or lender.
Apply for a suitable business loan and submit documents.
The lender appraises the proposal and, if eligible, seeks guarantee coverage.
Follow the lender's sanction and disbursement process.
caution: CGTMSE provides a guarantee to the lender; it does not directly lend money to the business. The guarantee ceiling is not an automatic loan entitlement.

name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
statusNote: Live scheme applied on the KVIC PMEGP portal, with subsidy processed under scheme rules.
maxAmountText: Project cost: manufacturing up to ₹50 lakh; services up to ₹20 lakh
purpose: Bank finance and margin-money subsidy for eligible new micro-enterprises.
documents: Aadhaar, PAN, photograph and bank details
Other documents requested by the portal or bank
process: Register on the PMEGP portal.
Submit the application and project report.
The implementing agency processes the proposal.
The bank assesses the loan; eligible subsidy is processed under scheme rules.
caution: Project cost is not the same as the bank loan amount. Subsidy depends on category, location and applicable guidelines.

name: SIDBI Business Loans
statusNote: Live lender with its own portal; limits are product-specific, so there is no single maximum amount.
purpose: Eligible machinery, expansion, working-capital, modernisation and other business finance.
documents: Bank statements and ITRs, where applicable
Project report, cash-flow projections and quotations
process: Select a relevant SIDBI product.
Apply online or through the relevant channel.
Submit financial and legal documents.
Complete credit/project appraisal and sanction formalities.
portalNote: Choose the relevant SIDBI product first; amount and conditions are set product by product.
caution: There is no single maximum amount applicable to all SIDBI products.

name: Regular Bank Term Loan
statusNote: Ordinary bank product, available from banks but with bank-specific amounts and terms.
purpose: Machinery, expansion, renovation, equipment and other capital expenditure.
documents: Bank statements, ITRs and financial statements, as applicable
process: Select a bank and suitable term-loan product.
Submit the application and documents.
Complete credit appraisal and any security checks.
Meet sanction conditions; the bank disburses if approved.
portalNote: Examples given by the source: https://sbi.bank.in/ and https://www.bankofbaroda.in - apply with the bank you choose.
caution: Loan amount, rate, tenure and collateral requirements vary by lender.

name: Working Capital / Cash Credit / Overdraft
statusNote: Everyday bank credit facility; the limit is fixed by the bank after assessing your business.
purpose: Stock, raw materials, supplier payments, salaries and daily operating expenses.
documents: Financial statements and existing borrowing details
process: Estimate the working-capital requirement.
Apply to the bank and submit records.
The bank assesses cash flow and working-capital needs.
The bank sets the limit and terms if approved.
portalNote: Apply through the selected bank's official website or branch.
caution: Cash credit and overdraft are credit facilities; their limits are assessed by the lender.

name: Invoice Financing / TReDS
statusNote: Live online platform where financiers bid on your unpaid invoices; funds depend on invoice value and offers.
maxAmountText: Based on eligible invoices and financier offer
purpose: Finance against eligible unpaid business invoices.
process: Register on a participating TReDS platform.
Upload an eligible invoice.
The buyer confirms the invoice.
Financiers make offers; accept an offer to receive funds under agreed terms.
portalNote: Portal listed as RXIL, a participating TReDS platform; platform/product rules apply.
caution: TReDS is a financing platform, not itself a government loan or subsidy.

name: Stand-Up India
statusNote: The source lists only the historical limit and says to verify the current application window before presenting it as open.
maxAmountText: Historical scheme limit: ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore; verify current availability
purpose: Historically supported eligible greenfield enterprises promoted by women and SC/ST entrepreneurs.
documents: Bank statements and quotations, where applicable
process: Check current scheme availability and guidelines.
Approach a participating bank or official channel.
Submit the proposal and documents.
Complete appraisal and sanction requirements.
caution: Verify the current application window before presenting this as open for new applications.

name: Micro-enterprise Credit Card (Budget 2025 announcement)
statusNote: Announced in Budget 2025 with a ₹5 lakh limit; it is not an automatic entitlement and lender availability must be checked.
purpose: Business-related credit needs for eligible Udyam-registered micro-enterprises.
documents: Bank and credit information required by issuer
Other documents requested by participating lender
process: Check whether a participating bank offers the product.
Apply through the lender.
Submit Udyam and KYC details.
The issuer verifies eligibility and sets any approved limit.
portalNote: Check participating-bank availability and current official announcements.
caution: The ₹5 lakh limit was announced in Budget 2025; it is not an automatic entitlement.

name: PM Vishwakarma Scheme
statusNote: Live scheme registered through Common Service Centres, with credit in two tranches.
maxAmountText: Up to ₹3 lakh: first tranche ₹1 lakh; second tranche ₹2 lakh
purpose: Concessional credit and other support for eligible traditional artisans and craftspeople.
documents: Ration card and/or other verification documents as required
process: Visit a participating Common Service Centre (CSC).
Complete Aadhaar-based authentication and registration.
Select the eligible traditional trade.
Complete verification and apply for the applicable credit tranche.
caution: Beneficiary interest rate is 5%, subject to scheme rules.

name: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)
statusNote: Live scheme for street vendors, with the source recording the lending period extended to 31 March 2030.
purpose: Working capital for eligible street vendors.
documents: Vendor identification/certificate of vending or letter of recommendation, as applicable
process: Check eligibility with the local urban authority or scheme portal.
Submit application and vendor/KYC documents.
The lender verifies eligibility.
Receive and repay the approved tranche under its terms.
caution: The scheme's lending period has been extended to 31 March 2030; verify current tranche rules before applying.

name: Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSMEs (MCGS-MSME)
statusNote: Live guarantee scheme routed through participating lending institutions.
purpose: Credit for eligible purchase of plant, machinery and equipment.
documents: Project report, bank statements and financial records
process: Approach a participating lending institution.
Submit the equipment-finance proposal.
The lender checks eligibility and viability.
Eligible guarantee coverage and loan sanction are processed by the lender.
caution: ₹100 crore is a credit ceiling under the scheme, not a guaranteed loan amount to every business.

name: Export Working Capital Finance
statusNote: Live export-finance product from EXIM Bank and commercial banks; limits are lender-specific.
purpose: Eligible financing for export production, shipment preparation and export transactions.
documents: Export order or letter of credit
Invoices and shipment documents, as applicable
PAN/KYC, Udyam, bank statements and financial records
process: Approach an authorised bank or export-finance provider.
Submit the export order and finance request.
The lender verifies transaction and business finances.
Complete sanction formalities and use funds for the approved purpose.
portalNote: Portal listed as EXIM Bank https://www.eximbankindia.in/ or participating commercial banks.
caution: Limits and product eligibility depend on the lender and export transaction.

name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Exporters (CGSE)
statusNote: The source gives no fixed amount and says scheme guidelines and availability must be checked with the participating lender.
maxAmountText: Additional credit support may be available under scheme limits; confirm operative guidelines
purpose: Additional credit support for eligible exporters under the notified scheme.
process: Contact the existing working-capital lender.
Ask whether the facility qualifies under the scheme.
Submit the export records and additional-credit request.
The lender checks eligibility and processes any applicable guarantee coverage.
portalNote: Accessed through participating banks; scheme information at https://www.ncgtc.in.
caution: Scheme guidelines and availability should be checked with the participating lender before advertising a specific limit.

name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
statusNote: Live credit-linked subsidy scheme; the source says subsidy and application availability depend on current guidelines.
maxAmountText: Credit-linked subsidy generally 35% of eligible project cost, capped at ₹10 lakh per eligible individual unit
purpose: Formalisation, upgrading and expansion of eligible micro food-processing units.
documents: Relevant food-business licences and other scheme documents
process: Check unit and project eligibility.
Apply through the designated scheme channel.
Submit project and supporting documents.
Bank assesses the loan; eligible subsidy is processed under scheme rules.
caution: A subsidy is not the same as a loan, and current application windows must be verified.

name: Startup Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGSS)
statusNote: Live guarantee scheme for DPIIT-recognised startups, reached through eligible lending institutions.
maxAmountText: Eligible credit guarantee up to ₹20 crore (scheme ceiling; not automatic credit)
purpose: Credit guarantee support for eligible DPIIT-recognised startups.
process: Check startup recognition and scheme eligibility.
Approach an eligible lending institution.
Submit the loan proposal and documents.
Lender assesses the proposal and processes eligible guarantee coverage.
caution: Guarantee coverage is not a direct loan or a guarantee that the lender will approve a specific amount.

name: Machinery and Equipment Loan
statusNote: Available from SIDBI or a participating bank as an ordinary equipment-finance product.
purpose: Purchase or upgrade business machinery and equipment.
documents: Project report and other lender-required documents
process: Obtain a supplier quotation.
Apply for equipment finance.
Submit the quotation and financial records.
The lender appraises the proposal and disburses if sanctioned.
portalNote: Source lists SIDBI https://www.sidbi.in/ or a participating bank.
caution: This is a bank product category, not one single government scheme.

name: Commercial Vehicle Loan
statusNote: Ordinary vehicle-finance product offered by banks and selected vehicle-finance lenders.
purpose: Purchase of eligible commercial vehicles for business use.
documents: Bank statements and ITRs, where applicable
Business proof and other lender-required documents
process: Select a commercial vehicle.
Apply through a lender.
Submit business and vehicle documents.
Complete appraisal, margin, registration and insurance formalities.
portalNote: Source lists Bank of Baroda https://www.bankofbaroda.in/ or a selected vehicle-finance lender.
caution: Loan amount and terms depend on the lender and vehicle.

name: Purchase Order Finance
statusNote: The source warns that availability depends on the provider and not all banks offer purchase-order finance.
purpose: Finance raw materials or costs to fulfil a confirmed customer order.
process: Submit the purchase order and fulfilment-cost estimate.
Financier verifies the order and customer.
The provider assesses business viability and repayment source.
Funds are released if the facility is approved.
portalNote: Apply through a bank or eligible business-finance provider.
caution: Availability depends on the provider; not all banks offer purchase-order finance.

name: Business Loan for Traders and Retailers
statusNote: Broad bank-product category sold by banks such as SBI; limits and terms vary by lender.
purpose: Eligible business expenses, inventory, expansion and operating needs.
documents: Financial statements and other lender-required documents
process: Select a suitable trader/business loan.
Submit the application and documents.
The lender checks turnover, cash flow and existing liabilities.
Complete appraisal and sanction requirements.
portalNote: Source lists SBI https://sbi.bank.in/ or the selected bank's official business-loan portal.
caution: This is a broad bank-product category; limits and terms vary by lender.

source: MSME Loans & Credit Schemes - Avishkaar reference (FY 2025-26)
safeguards: Show whether a product is currently open for applications, announced but awaiting implementation, or subject to confirmation.
Store the official portal, lender, last-verified date, eligibility conditions, documents and source for each product.
Separate direct loans from credit-guarantee schemes, subsidies, invoice financing and ordinary bank products.
Do not promise approval, a specific interest rate or a maximum loan amount unless confirmed by the lender.
Collect only necessary personal and financial documents, obtain user consent, and protect sensitive information.
Make clear that the bank/lender makes the final credit decision.
